chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

regarding the false testifier: 'What is his repentance?' He said: 'He pays from the wealth concerning which he testified against [the victim], in proportion to what was taken from his wealth — whether it was the half or the third — if this one testified and another one was with him.'

key_terms.بِقَدْرِ: in proportion/measure — indicating proportional liability among multiple false witnesses
key_terms.تَوْبَة: repentance — in Islamic law, sincere turning away from sin, which for violations of others' rights requires restitution
key_terms.شَاهِدُ الزُّورِ: false witness — one who testifies falsely in a legal proceeding
key_terms.يُؤَدِّي: pays/restores — the legal obligation to return or compensate

ai.seo_question: What is the repentance of a false witness according to Imam al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that the repentance of a false witness (shahid al-zur) is not merely verbal but requires material restitution: the false witness must compensate the victim for the financial harm caused by the false testimony. The ruling specifies proportional liability — if there were two false witnesses, each is responsible for his proportional share (one-half each). This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that valid repentance (tawba) for sins involving the rights of others (huquq al-nas) requires both cessation of the sin and restoration of any harm caused.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the false testifier, what is his repentance?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would pay from his wealth to the one whom he had testified against by the measurement of what had gone from his wealth, whether it was the half, or the third, if this one had testified and another one was with him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash ‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following:

“About the case of a man who testifies falsely and upon his repenting, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘He must pay for the assets that are gone due to his false testimony, like one-half or one-third if another one has testified with him.’”
